chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim and 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who died during a journey while no women and no mahram were with her. He said: The places of wudu (ablution) are to be washed from her, salat (prayer) is to be performed over her, and she is to be buried.

key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman; the deceased female subject of the ruling
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a mahram male relative with whom marriage is forbidden
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel; the circumstance in which the death occurred
key_terms.مَوْضِعُ الْوُضُوءِ: the bodily areas normally washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهَا: the funeral salat (prayer) is performed over her

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a woman dies during travel and no women or mahram are present to wash her body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for the case of a woman who dies while traveling and is not accompanied by any women or a mahram. In such a case, only the parts associated with wudu (ablution) are washed, then funeral salat (prayer) is performed over her, and she is buried.
